In algebraic topology, the '''Bousfield class''' of, say, a [[spectrum (topology)|spectrum]] ''X'' is the set of all (say) spectra ''Y'' whose [[smash product]] with ''X'' is zero: <math>X \otimes Y = 0</math>. Two objects are '''Bousfield equivalent''' if their Bousfield classes are the same.

The notion applies to [[module spectrum|module spectra]] and in that case one usually qualifies a ring spectrum over which the smash product is taken.
